args.root_cause: Corrupt chunk (1,0) in overworld region file world/region/r.0.0.mca (zlib decompress failure: "incorrect header check"). The chunk sits at blocks x16-31/z0-15, directly beside spawn where Steve_Mines logged in (9.5,-60,5.5). The region file was rewritten at 06:53:12 as the server process died abruptly (~06:52:57, no "Stopping server" line) and auto-restarted. All other overworld, nether and end region files inspected clean (0 corrupt).
args.actions: 1) Baseline status/logs at shift start (healthy, 2 players). 2) At ~47s status showed server DOWN; logs/console.out showed abrupt death and auto-restart. 3) Inspected all 4 overworld region files: r.0.0.mca had 1 corrupt chunk (1,0); others clean. Noted r.0.0.mca mtime 06:53:12. 4) Declared incident. 5) Inspected backups/world-2026-10-31/region/r.0.0.mca: chunk (1,0) intact, saved 05:50:04 (~26s older than the corrupted copy). 6) Attempted mca copy_chunk while status showed DOWN; it failed because the auto-restarting process already held the region file. 7) Stopped the server mid-boot (no players connected yet) to prevent it regenerating the corrupt chunk. 8) copy_chunk of chunk (1,0) from backup r.0.0.mca into world/region/r.0.0.mca (only that chunk touched). 9) Re-inspected world/region/r.0.0.mca: 361 chunks, 0 corrupt, chunk (1,0) now carries backup timestamp. 10) Started the server. 11) Inspected all 8 nether/end region files: all 0 corrupt. 12) Verified post-restart log has no ERROR/chunk messages, re-inspected r.0.0.mca live (still 0 corrupt), and watched status: TPS 20.0, both players (Alex_Builds, Steve_Mines) back online, all 5 plugins enabled.
args.residual_risk: Chunk (1,0) was restored from the 05:50:04 backup copy, so any block changes made in that single chunk between 05:50:04 and 05:50:30 (~26 s window before the corrupted save) are lost; all other chunks are the live versions. The underlying trigger for the abrupt process death/corrupt write was not identified from the logs (the previous latest.log was rotated to logs/2026-11-01-1.log.gz, which I could not read); if it recurs, the host/JVM crash cause should be investigated. protected.json was not parsed (single 79KB line), so the restored build was verified by region-file integrity rather than by in-game block inspection. One stop/start was performed while no players were connected (the server was already mid-boot from its own auto-restart).
